wy_big_bird_area.blurb: A small wall in Tongue River Canyon outside Dayton, in the eastern Bighorns, with ten climbs split between gear routes and bolted lines. A large roof with a smaller one beside it makes the face easy to spot from the trail. Grades run from easy fifth class through the 5.10s, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.10 range and only one harder sport line, so it suits climbers building up. The canyon's walls face south, which makes them hot in midsummer and pleasantly warm in late winter and early spring. Crowds are thin; you are more likely to share the canyon with anglers than with a queue at a route.

wy_central.blurb: The middle stretch of the Bridge Bands, a south-facing crag in Shoshone Canyon just west of Cody. It sits on the second tier, east of the Cowboy Wall, and holds ten climbs: seven sport and three trad. Grades are friendly, from 5.5 up to 5.10, with a handful in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, so it works well for newer leaders and moderate mileage days. The cliff is mostly slabby on the lower pitches with steeper ground higher up, and the rock can feel prickly. The walk from the highway parking lot is short, a matter of minutes.

wy_dome_rock_pedro_mountains.blurb: A granite dome on the high plains south of Alcova, around 8,500 feet, and a regular outing for climbers from Casper. The rock is weathered clean and mostly sound, though fracturing has left some loose blocks here and there. Ten climbs are listed: seven boulder problems and three trad lines. The problems start at beginner level around V2 and climb to a few very hard ones, while the trad routes range from easy to hard. The established crack lines are mostly moderate, on walls of roughly 250 feet that sit a little shy of vertical. Bring a rack and a pad.

wy_friend_creek_pinnacle_region.blurb: A pinnacle and ridge high on Laramie Peak in the Laramie Range, around 8,450 feet, reached by walking the summit trail and then branching a short distance off it. All ten climbs here are trad, mostly hand and finger cracks in fine-grained granite that breaks into large blocks, with few face holds. Grades lean toward 5.10 and 5.11, with a couple of easier 5.8s and one 5.12. Nuts and cams both fit the cracks well. The elevation makes it a pleasant escape in warm months, and the ridge has more unclimbed cracks waiting.

wy_matrix_pillar.blurb: A nearly freestanding pillar on the east side of the French Cattle Ranch in upper Ten Sleep Canyon, with short routes on every side. All ten are sport climbs, running from 5.9 to 5.12 with five in the 5.11 range, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. The east face holds a lot of shade, and the big dihedral there stays cooler than the cliffs around it, which helps on warm days. The routes are compact, and the pillar can be walked around to pick a line that fits the day's sun.

wy_mushroom_tip_wall.blurb: A short, powerful sport wall at Crag 6, the high-country sector sitting on top of the Bighorn Mountains above Ten Sleep Canyon. Ten bolted routes, mostly boulder-problem hard, with five in the 5.13 range, two at 5.14, and a few 5.12s and one 5.11 to warm up on. It is a place for strong climbers rather than beginners, since moderate options are scarce. Crag 6 as a whole is a summer destination and tends to fill up on busy days, so expect company on the well-known lines.
